_comment: Configuration template for the eMaster Gateway (request/release.md section 5).
The gateway stores its live configuration in a SQLite database, config/config.db,
one row per section. On the FIRST start against a path with no database, if a
sibling <name>.json is found it is imported once to seed it -- so copying this
file to config/config.json is the supported way to preload settings:
After that first start, config.db is the source of truth and the JSON file is
ignored; edit settings from the web UI's Configuration page instead.
config.db and config.json are both gitignored: they hold the REST API key, and
clients.db holds generated per-client card-reader keys. Never commit them.
Replace every YOUR_* placeholder below before use.

system._comment: Identity of this installation. Nothing in the C++ reads these -- they exist so scripts can ask for Config.Get("system.machine_id") instead of hard-coding it.

web._comment: Dashboard HTTP + WebSocket server. 0.0.0.0 listens on every interface; use 127.0.0.1 to restrict to the local machine. locker_ui_* is the SmartLocker floor plan (web/locker/), served on its OWN port so a kiosk or a firewall can be pointed at exactly one of the two UIs; it reads locker_db_path read-only and pushes state over a WebSocket at /ws.

rest._comment: Upstream REST server the gateway reports to. api_key is sent as the API-Key header.

serial._comment: Citizen ID card reader. Windows: COM3. Linux: /dev/ttyUSB0. macOS: /dev/cu.usbserial-XXXX.

serial2._comment: TDM-800 LED display (request/LEDBoard.md). Opened by led.lua, not at startup.

modbus._comment: Modbus TCP PLC. Coils (FC01/FC05) and discrete inputs (FC02) are SEPARATE address spaces -- see Modbus.RegisterInput's source argument in the Lua API docs if a dashboard input never changes.

rfid._comment: Card reader. mode is one of: tcp_json (JSON payload, reads the 'Raw' field), zk (ZKTeco PullSDK -- Windows x86 builds only), or disabled.

zk._comment: ZKTeco access controller the Lua workflow reads card UIDs from, via zk.connect(). Separate from `rfid` above because they are two different devices; nothing in the backend connects to this one. Read from Lua as Config.Get("zk.ip").
zk._comment_backend: Which protocol reaches the panel. 'auto' uses the ZKTeco PullSDK DLL where it is compiled in (32-bit Windows only) and the panel's own C3 TCP protocol everywhere else -- so a Linux gateway gets working doors instead of NotSupportedOnThisPlatform. Force 'c3' on Windows too if you would rather not depend on the vendor DLL; 'pullsdk' fails anywhere the DLL cannot load.

card_api._comment: Master switch for POST /api/card/input. When false that endpoint returns 403 regardless of stored client keys. Manage per-client keys from Test Tools > Card Clients.

lua._comment: Startup script, relative to config/scripts/. Empty means no script runs at boot. Further scripts are started from the Lua Editor; several can run at once.

logging._comment: Structured business logs written by Log.Write() into config/logs.db, searchable on the Logs page. The runtime log (Log.Info and friends) is a rotating file plus an in-memory buffer and needs no configuration. retention_days 0 keeps everything; pruning runs at startup. definitions_path is relative to this config directory.

auth._comment: API authentication, RBAC, brute-force lockout and rate limiting. Unlike every other feature switch here, `enabled` defaults TRUE -- an authentication system that has to be switched on protects nobody. Accounts live in config/security.db; on first start the gateway seeds one ADMIN and prints its one-time password to the console. Turning this off leaves every endpoint on the web port open to anyone who can reach it; see docs/security.md before you do. token_lifetime_sec is the bearer token lifetime, max_failed_attempts/lockout_seconds the per-account lockout, and the *_rate_per_sec/*_burst pairs are token buckets per source IP.

plugins._comment: Plugin configuration and desired startup state. Enable/Disable in Plugin Manager updates the enabled field. The database is outside the firmware release, so these choices survive software updates.

update._comment: Over-the-air updates. Off by default -- turning it on is you choosing which release server this device trusts. The gateway polls `url` for a manifest and offers what it finds in a popup; nothing installs without a click. Packages are checked against the manifest SHA-256 and a detached signature over <version>\n<platform>\n<sha256>, and a release that fails to start is rolled back. Requires the managed layout scripts/install-ota.sh creates. See docs/ota-update.md.
